objectClass.notes: The coils must read as woven straw volume, not smooth yellow pottery. The three hive profiles and entrances must remain individually readable.

reasoning: Three similar but non-identical organic profiles require controlled variation instead of simple duplication.
Fifty-four visible coils, bindings, entrances, symbols, honeycomb cells and bees create high repetition density.
The lower tool layer is prone to bench occlusion and therefore requires direct main-view review and repositioning.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required by the straw construction, three individualized hives, cloth cap, multi-part bench and beekeeper tool set.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Hive interiors remain dark implied cavities rather than boolean cut-throughs.
Bees are restrained symbolic-scale meshes rather than particle sprites.

details.description: Three hives use unequal height, radius and shoulder profiles rather than scaled duplicates.
Each hive carries eighteen projected straw coils with slight radius and color variation.
Short vertical binding stitches interrupt the horizontal coil rhythm.
All three hives have dark arched entrances with thick straw rope trim.
Separate oak landing boards project below each entrance with visible nails.
Three number-free carved symbols distinguish the hives beside their entrances.
The smallest hive carries a faded red waxed-cloth cap with irregular draped hem.
Two rope ties pull the cloth cap down against the straw body.
Nine top planks sit on two long runners with projected nails and a lower shelf.
Four mossed limestone feet isolate the bench from damp meadow ground.
A clay water dish contains a recessed clear surface and eight stepping pebbles.
A black iron smoker uses three cage rings, eight rails, cone spout, leather bellows and smoke wisps.
A framed comb contains more than forty separate hexagonal wax cells and amber drops.
A separate clay crock exposes amber honey beneath a cloth cover and rope tie.
Eight restrained worker bees use striped bodies and paired translucent wings around entrances.

anatomy.note: Object domain; tiny bees are decorative subcomponents, not character reconstruction targets.

definitionOfDone: Three individualized woven hives, entrances, cap, bench and a visible beekeeper tool layer remain readable in main and side review.

qualityCriteria: Three unequal hive profiles and entrance positions remain distinct.
Projected coils, bindings and rough straw response prevent pottery read.
Water dish, smoker, comb and crock remain visible instead of being hidden by the bench.
Straw, oak, stone, cloth, iron, leather, clay, water, wax and honey respond independently.

antiShallowSpecRules: No three yellow spheres may pass as skeps.
The tool layer may not be hidden behind the bench.
The cloth cap may not be a rigid cone.

authoringInstruction: Assessment completed from the admitted reference and a direct browser correction that moved the occluded tool layer into view.
